key_insight: The paper shows that tensor-network compression can reformulate Carr-Madan option pricing so Fourier-based pricing scales much better without explicitly building exponentially large vectors or transforms.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to large-scale financial simulation by reducing memory bottlenecks and enabling scalable pricing on both classical and quantum workflows.
method: Use tensor networks to tensorize the option-pricing problem.
Apply the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT), a compressed Tensor Train form of the QFT.
Compare classical tensor-network pricing with QFT-based simulations on quantum simulators and hardware.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on European call options report preserved pricing accuracy, lower memory use, and subexponential scaling versus conventional FFT-based pricing.
watch_item: Performance depends on tensor-network compression quality and implementation details, so scaling gains may weaken for less structured or poorly compressible problems.
paper_title: Classical Tensor Network and Quantum Fourier Transform Approaches for Large-Scale Carr-Madan Option Pricing
